properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-22: every link of the founding chain EXISTS as a served tool, and the chain has never once been walked on reflow2's own design — 0 checks have ever been recorded failing, so the loop's entry point has never fired
properties.statement:
ANTHONY'S FOUNDING CHAIN, in his words on 2026-09-22, and the reason he built reflow2: "testing discovers a failure → root cause analysis identifies that changes are required in subsystem A → reflow2 sees that by changing subsystem A, it'll require changes to the interface contract between subsystem A and subsystem B also → reflow2 updates design in all places and ensures that all requirements are still met."

His doubt, stated the same day: reflow2 is near fielded, its own testing is inadequately described in the design, "the chain I showed earlier is missing inside reflow2 — and if reflow2 isn't doing it for itself, then how can I assume it isn't doing it for other reflow2 designs?"

⭐ THE DOUBT IS CORRECT, AND THE PRECISE FORM IS DIFFERENT FROM — AND MORE ACTIONABLE THAN — THE GENERAL ONE. It is NOT that the chain is missing. Every link exists as a served tool. It is that THE CHAIN HAS NEVER BEEN WALKED, and two of its links stand on substrate too thin to carry it.

═══ LINK BY LINK, MEASURED ═══

① TESTING DISCOVERS A FAILURE → `reconcile_verification` EXISTS, and its own description calls it "the P4 reconcile, LAST OF THE THREE FEEDBACK LOOPS (BL-30)": supply what a real run reported, and "a recorded 'passing' that the run FAILED is the dangerous direction and sorts first — the design believed proven what is actually broken." That is his vision, built.
    🛑 AND IT HAS APPARENTLY NEVER BEEN USED HERE. Verifications: 311 `passing`, 1 `planned`, **0 `failing`**. Not one check in this design's history has ever been recorded as having failed. 46 have never run at all; 282 of 312 have no executable form. THE ENTRY POINT OF THE FOUNDING CHAIN HAS NEVER FIRED ON REFLOW2 ITSELF.

② ROOT CAUSE → the root-cause skill and `record_finding` with `caused_by` + `cause_evidence` exist, and a detector reports a fix joined to no cause. Measured 2026-09-06: **183 of 209 fixes were joined to no cause.** The link exists and carries about one repair in eight.

③ A CHANGE IN A REACHES THE A↔B CONTRACT → `propagate_change` exists and walks the golden thread. But it can only flag a contract that is MODELLED, and the seams band is the design's own frontier: **contracts declared for 13 of 72 couplings (18%)**, 22 Interfaces against 108 Components. For roughly four couplings in five there is no A↔B node for the propagation to reach.

④ REFLOW2 UPDATES THE DESIGN IN ALL PLACES → this one is genuinely NOT built and should not be claimed. `propagate_change` REPORTS a blast radius; a person or an agent then edits. Nothing applies a change across the affected set.

⑤ ALL REQUIREMENTS STILL MET → the delivery line computes this from the thread and `detect_gaps` reports what broke. This link works.

═══ ⚠️ THE LADDER HE THINKS IS MISSING IS PRESENT, AND THAT MATTERS ═══

He wrote that the flow "concept → requirements → capabilities" ends there and should continue to "tested/verified/validated → fielded/operational". THE VOCABULARY IS ALREADY THERE: Capability.status runs planned → in_progress → realized → verified, and `maturity_report` reports seven bands — intent, function, allocation, seams, realization, assurance, operation — with operation at 99% (73 of 74 releases deployed to a declared environment). So the ladder exists and is read.
    ⇒ WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT THE RUNGS BUT THE DRIVE. Nothing MOVES a capability up the ladder on evidence. A capability reaches `verified` because somebody typed it, not because a run said so — which is the same defect as ①, seen from the other end.

═══ 🛑 WHY THIS IS A FAIR CRITICISM OF REFLOW2 AND NOT ONLY OF THIS REPOSITORY ═══

His inference — if it does not do this for itself, why assume it does for others — is sound, and the mechanism explains it. Every leg above is OPT-IN. `reconcile_verification` must be called; a cause must be attached; a contract must be declared. Nothing requires them, and nothing reports their absence at a level that changes behaviour. So a consuming project gets exactly what this one got: a complete toolkit, no drive, and a design that looks verified because 311 checks say `passing`.
    ⭐ AND REFLOW2 CANNOT CURRENTLY TELL WHETHER ANY CONSUMER EVER CLOSED THE LOOP. There is no reading anywhere that says "this design has never fed a test result back".

═══ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED ═══

Whether `reconcile_verification` has literally never been called, or has been called and always agreed. The design records no DriftEvent of verification kind and no failing check, which is consistent with both; distinguishing them needs the usage ledger, which counts tool calls and was not consulted for this finding. The stronger claim — that the loop has never been CLOSED — rests on 0 failing checks in 312, which is decisive on its own.
